paragraphs: Here's what I think this passage is about, friend. The LORD is the potter, and we are the clay. He says, "Just like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel" (Jeremiah 18:6). That's not a threat. The potter is not scared of a flawed pot, and he doesn't toss the clay out. He works with it.

And the clay gets a say in how this goes. The LORD says that if a nation He warned turns from its evil, then He "will relent of the disaster I had planned to bring" (Jeremiah 18:8). So the door to turn back is open, and He tells Judah, "Turn now, each of you, from your evil ways, and correct your ways and deeds" (Jeremiah 18:11). But they answer, "It is hopeless" (Jeremiah 18:12). Friend, the hopeless part was never on the LORD's side of the wheel.

So why does it matter to you? Because turning is always on the table, and the LORD gets to shape you while you're still soft. I can't tell you how many times I've wanted to grab my own lopsided edges and say, I'm too far gone. Don't. Jeremiah brings his hurt to the LORD, and I think that shows where to take it: straight to Him, honest and out loud. Stay soft, baker, and let the Potter work.
